source_evidence: A market order is an order to buy or sell a security immediately. This type of order guarantees that the order will be executed, but does not guarantee the execution price.
answer: A market order tells a broker to buy or sell a security immediately. It guarantees execution, but not the price you will receive or pay. The order generally executes at or near the current ask price when buying or bid price when selling, so the last-traded price may not be the execution price.
